newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end down, off lows, in jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end down, off lows, in jittery trade.

text.p: Shares fell at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Wednesday rocked by rumours the enforcement directorate had arrested top ITC officials, brokers said.
A spokeswoman for the tobacco and hotel conglomerate said one official and three former employees were detained by the enforcement directorate for questioning.
She denied rumours that some directors were arrested.
ITC share fell 18.25 rupees, or 5.68 percent, to 303.
Senior ITC officials have been accused of violations of India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act in connection with some of the firm's export deals.
The firm also has a long-standing dispute with federal tax authorities over excise payments.
Brokers said the enforcement raid rumours triggered speculative selling pressure and unnerved players.
The 30-share BSE index ended 66.96 points, or 2.07 percent, lower at 3,172.98 after sliding to 3,163.40.
The 500-stock CRISIL index finished at a provisional 610.18 against Tuesday's 619.76 close.
There was no trading at the National exchange due to a technical snag, the bourse said.
Traders said foreign funds were shaken by the ITC news and stayed on the sidelines.

Institutional players were reluctant to make commitments ahead of crucial company results this week, traders said. TISCO ended 4.0 rupees lower at 186.75. Traders expect the steel firm to report net profit of 2.3-2.5 billion rupees in the first six months to September 30 against 2.01 billion in year-ago period.
Thermax edged up 0.75 rupees to 346.75 after it said first half net profit rose 31 percent to 199.2 million rupees.
L&T dropped 5.25 rupees to 224.25, SBI 4.75 to 230.25, Reliance 4.50 to 205.50 and Hind Lever 11.75 to 792.
